name: Leontes
description: King of Sicilia. Seized by a sudden, groundless jealousy that his pregnant wife Hermione loves his boyhood friend Polixenes, he orders Polixenes poisoned, imprisons Hermione, defies Apollo's oracle, and so causes the death of his son Mamillius, the apparent death of his wife, and the casting-away of his newborn daughter. Sixteen years of penance later, daughter and wife are miraculously restored to him.

name: Hermione
description: Queen of Sicilia, wife of Leontes, falsely accused of adultery with Polixenes. Pregnant at her arrest, she bears a daughter in prison, defends herself with grave dignity at her trial, and collapses at the news of her son's death. Reported dead, she is kept hidden by Paulina for sixteen years and revealed at the close as a living 'statue.'

name: Polixenes
description: King of Bohemia and Leontes's boyhood friend, whose long visit triggers Leontes's jealousy. Warned by Camillo that Leontes means to poison him, he flees home. Sixteen years later he furiously opposes his son Florizel's love for the shepherdess Perdita — not knowing she is a princess.

name: Camillo
description: An honest Sicilian lord. Ordered to poison Polixenes, he warns him instead and flees with him to Bohemia, where he serves sixteen years. Homesick, he helps the eloping Florizel and Perdita to Sicilia, engineering the reunions that end the play.

name: Paulina
description: A great-hearted noblewoman, wife of Antigonus and Hermione's fearless champion. She denounces Leontes to his face, brings him the newborn princess, and after the queen's reported death keeps her secretly alive for sixteen years, finally staging the 'awakening' of Hermione's statue.

name: Perdita
description: The lost daughter ('Perdita') of Leontes and Hermione, abandoned as an infant on the Bohemian coast and raised by an old shepherd. Grown into a queen of the sheep-shearing feast, she is loved by Prince Florizel; her royal birth is revealed and she is restored to her parents.

name: Florizel
description: Prince of Bohemia, son of Polixenes. Wooing the shepherdess Perdita under the name 'Doricles,' he defies his father's rage and flees with her to Sicilia, where her true parentage is discovered and their match blessed.

name: Autolycus
description: A roguish peddler, ballad-seller, and pickpocket — once in Prince Florizel's service. A merry trickster, he robs the Clown, fleeces the shepherds at the sheep-shearing, and stumbles his way into helping the plot toward its happy end.

name: Shepherd
description: The old shepherd who finds the abandoned baby Perdita with her gold and tokens and raises her as his own — meeting 'things new-born' as Antigonus meets 'things dying.' His honest household hosts the sheep-shearing feast.

name: Clown
description: The old Shepherd's son, a good-natured simpleton who witnesses the shipwreck and the bear, is gulled and robbed by Autolycus, and is raised to gentility when Perdita's royalty is revealed.

name: Antigonus
description: A Sicilian lord, husband of Paulina. Forced to swear he will abandon the infant princess, he carries her to the Bohemian coast, lays her down with gold and a name, and makes his celebrated exit 'pursued by a bear.'

name: Mamillius
description: The young prince of Sicilia, Leontes and Hermione's son, who begins to tell a 'sad tale... of sprites and goblins.' He sickens at his mother's disgrace and dies — the innocent casualty of his father's jealousy.

name: Time
description: Time, personified as the Chorus, who steps forward at the opening of Act 4 to 'slide o'er sixteen years,' turning his glass to carry the story from Leontes's grief in Sicilia to Perdita grown up in Bohemia. The hinge of the play's two halves.

name: Archidamus
description: A lord of Bohemia who, in the opening scene, trades courtesies with Camillo about the friendship of the two kings.

name: Cleomenes
description: A Sicilian lord sent with Dion to consult Apollo's oracle at Delphos; later he urges the penitent Leontes to forgive himself.

name: Dion
description: A Sicilian lord sent with Cleomenes to the oracle at Delphos.

name: Emilia
description: A lady attending the imprisoned Hermione, who carries news between the queen and Paulina.

name: Mopsa
description: A shepherdess at the sheep-shearing, courted by the Clown and eager for Autolycus's ballads.

name: Dorcas
description: A shepherdess at the sheep-shearing feast who quarrels with Mopsa over the Clown.

name: First Lord
description: A lord of Sicilia attending Leontes.

name: Lord
description: An attending lord at the Sicilian court.

name: Lords
description: Sicilian lords speaking together.

name: First Lady
description: A lady attending Hermione, playing with the young Mamillius.

name: Second Lady
description: A lady attending Hermione.

name: First Gentleman
description: One of the gentlemen who report the wonders of the recognition and reunion in Act 5.

name: Second Gentleman
description: One of the gentlemen who narrate the off-stage reunions in Act 5.

name: Third Gentleman
description: The gentleman (Paulina's steward) who describes the meeting of the kings and the finding of Perdita in Act 5.

name: Gentleman
description: A gentleman of the Sicilian court.

name: Servant
description: A servant at court or at the shepherd's feast, announcing arrivals.

name: Officer
description: An officer of the court who reads the indictment at Hermione's trial.

name: Crier
description: The court crier who summons Hermione to her trial.

name: Keeper
description: The gaoler who keeps the imprisoned Hermione and reluctantly yields her baby to Paulina.

name: Mariner
description: The master of the ship that carries Antigonus and the baby to Bohemia, uneasy at the gathering storm.

name: First Attendant
description: An attendant at the Sicilian court.

name: Second Attendant
description: An attendant at the Sicilian court.
